recent_posts.title: Announcing Cohort 7 of the Ethereum Protocol Fellowship
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation has opened applications for the seventh cohort of the Ethereum Protocol Fellowship (EPF7). The program connects aspiring protocol developers with Ethereum's core R&D teams to contribute to client implementations, testing, specifications, and core protocol research. EPF7 will be a smaller, more focused cohort than previous iterations, emphasizing depth of engagement and closer mentor collaboration. Applications are open until May 13, with an introductory town hall on May 6 at 1500 UTC.

recent_posts.title: Allocation Update - Q1 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation's Q1 2026 allocation update details grants and funding across multiple categories including cryptography, zero-knowledge proofs, privacy, security, nodes and clients, Layer 2, and ecosystem development. Key funded projects include Lighthouse client development for the Fusaka transition, Poseidon cryptanalysis research, ZK formal verification tooling, privacy infrastructure (Kohaku SDK, Tor integration), Erigon zkEVM work, L2BEAT transparency dashboards, and developer education tools like BuidlGuidl. The allocations reflect EF's strategic priorities around ZK proof systems, protocol security, privacy, and developer tooling for 2026.

recent_posts.title: ETH Rangers Program Recap
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation, Secureum, The Red Guild, and SEAL have wrapped up the six-month ETH Rangers Program, which provided stipends to 17 individuals doing public goods security work. Key outcomes include over $5.8M in funds recovered or frozen, 785+ vulnerabilities reported, ~100 DPRK IT workers identified, 36+ incident responses handled, and 7+ open source security tools developed. Highlighted projects include DeFiHackLabs' incident explorer and education platform, the Ketman Project's DPRK infiltration investigations, Nick Bax's incident response and threat intelligence work, Guild Audits' smart contract security bootcamps across Africa and beyond, improvements to the Kontrol formal verification tool, and DoS vulnerability research across all five major Ethereum execution clients.

recent_posts.title: Checkpoint #9: Apr 2026
recent_posts.summary: Ethereum's Checkpoint #9 provides a status update on two upcoming protocol upgrades. Glamsterdam is in active development with devnets underway, featuring ePBS (encrypted Proposer-Builder Separation), Block-level Access Lists, gas repricings, and a likely increase to maximum contract size (EIP-7954). A first generalized Glamsterdam devnet is targeted for the near term, pending ePBS stabilization. The following upgrade, Hegotá, has selected FOCIL (EIP-7805) as its consensus layer headliner, while Account Abstraction (EIP-8141) was moved to Considered for Inclusion due to lack of consensus on implementation. Quantum resistance is gaining interest but lacks a standalone proposal. Gas limit testing is ongoing with a 60M baseline target. New EIP Champion's Handbook resources have been published to help contributors navigate the proposal process.

recent_posts.title: How L1 and L2s can Build the strongest possible Ethereum
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation's Platform team outlines an updated vision for the relationship between Ethereum L1 and L2 chains. The document argues that L1's role is to serve as a maximally resilient, permissionless hub for settlement, liquidity, and DeFi, while L2s should focus on differentiation, customization, and extending Ethereum's core properties to more users. Key recommendations for L2s include pursuing Stage 2 trustlessness, synchronous composability, and transparency about security properties. The EF commits to scaling L1 and blobs without sacrificing decentralization, investing in native rollup technology, improving cross-layer liquidity, and addressing ecosystem fragmentation through better interoperability solutions.

recent_posts.title: The Promise of Ethereum: Introducing the EF Mandate
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation has published the EF Mandate, a foundational document outlining the organization's mission, principles, and commitments. The mandate centers on preserving user self-sovereignty and ensuring Ethereum remains censorship-resistant, open source, private, and secure (CROPS). It clarifies the EF's role as one steward among many rather than a central authority, and has been published on-chain for anyone to read, reinterpret, and remix. The document is framed as a response to a rapidly changing world where AI-mediated environments and less accountable systems make Ethereum's original promise more relevant than ever.

recent_posts.title: Ethereum Foundation launches Project Odin to help public goods projects achieve funding sustainability
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation introduces Project Odin, a structured sustainability program for critical open-source public goods projects in the Ethereum ecosystem. The program embeds strategic advisors with grantee teams over 12 months to help them diversify funding beyond single grant sources, improve operational maturity, and build resilient funding portfolios. Vyper's smart contract language team, now operating as the Foundation for Verified Software, is the first pilot participant. The post outlines the three-phase engagement model (research, validation, execution), explains why funding diversification is treated as risk management, and introduces a longer-term vision for 'Frontier Research Contractors' — institutions that blend grants and contracts to sustain advanced technical work without the constraints of startups or large academic organizations.

recent_posts.title: Treasury Staking Initiative
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation has begun staking approximately 70,000 ETH from its treasury, using open-source tools Dirk (distributed signer across multiple geographic regions) and Vouch (multi-client support). The setup uses Type 2 (0x02) withdrawal credentials, enabling validator consolidation down to ~35 signing keys with a 2048 ETH max effective balance per validator. Infrastructure combines minority clients, hosted and self-managed hardware across jurisdictions, and builds blocks locally without proposer-builder separation. The initiative generates ETH-denominated yield for the foundation while demonstrating transparent, resilient solo staking practices.

recent_posts.title: The Ethereum Foundation's Commitment to DeFi
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation outlines its strategic commitment to decentralized finance (DeFi), articulating a vision of permissionless, censorship-resistant, privacy-first, and self-custodial financial systems. Two dedicated DeFi leads—Charles St. Louis and ivangbi—are introduced as heading the EF's DeFi efforts within the App Relations team. Key focus areas for 2026 include builder relationships, security improvements, decentralization, privacy as base infrastructure, standards and risk clarity, and research. The post also highlights emerging areas of interest such as DeFi × AI, institutional adoption, stablecoins, and novel financial primitives.

recent_posts.title: Protocol Priorities Update for 2026
recent_posts.summary: The Ethereum Foundation's Protocol team outlines its 2026 roadmap after a productive 2025 that saw two major network upgrades (Pectra and Fusaka), including PeerDAS mainnet deployment enabling an 8x increase in theoretical blob capacity. For 2026, work is reorganized into three tracks: Scale (merging L1 and blob scaling under Ansgar, Marius, and Raúl), Improve UX (focusing on native account abstraction via EIP-7701/EIP-8141 and cross-L2 interoperability, led by Barnabé and Matt), and a new Harden the L1 track (covering security, censorship resistance, and network resilience, led by Fredrik, Pari, and Thomas). The next major upgrade, Glamsterdam, is targeted for H1 2026, with Hegotá planned later in the year, aiming for parallel execution, higher gas limits, enshrined PBS, and post-quantum readiness.
